text:
maya: Heads-up — since last night we're seeing a steady shift toward streaming-first requests in EU. Median context length jumped ~2k -> ~6k tokens and streaming traffic volume is ~2.8x. Can we do a fast capacity + cost check before the afternoon deploy? Anyone on call?
igor: I'm on. Which pools are hot? any specific routes?
maya: Mostly routes served by dedicated-gpu-eu-w and hosted-eu-stream. Also saw a transient network blip on the peering link last night (10% packet loss for ~12m). Could be contributing to replays.
devon: Noted. KV cache miss rate for long contexts spiked from ~4% -> ~18% on those routes, so GPU work per request increased a lot.
igor: Pulling metrics now. Quick prom query I'm using:
```promql
sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{mode="stream",region="eu"}[5m])) by (pool)
```
igor: p99 latency for stream clients climbed from 210ms -> 380ms in the last 6h on dedicated-eu-w. Token/sec per GPU dropped ~22% due to larger contexts + miss rate.
elena: Quick cost projection: if this trend continues, EU GPU hours could increase ~24% over next 30 days (assuming same traffic shape). That maps to ~3.6k extra GPU hours for Dedicated EU month — ~estimated $27k delta if left unchecked.
maya: Oof. We need a mitigations plan that balances latency SLOs vs cost.
priya: A few low-risk mitigations to try: enable prefix/KV caching for streaming routes, reduce default chunk size from 2048 -> 1024 for EU stream routes, and turn on micro-batching for small streams. Should reduce tokens fed to the model and improve batching.
priya: Config snippet we can push as a canary:
```yaml
routes:
  - name: eu-chat-stream
    pool: hosted-eu-stream
    max_chunk_tokens: 1024
    prefix_cache: true
    micro_batch: true
```
devon: Agree. Also recommend increasing cache TTL for prefix entries to reduce repeated KV fills while we ride out the spike. Current TTL is 30m, bumping to 2h helps for conversational flows.
igor: I'll spin up a small canary: 2x p4d-eu nodes on the dedicated pool with quantized v2 model variant and run live traffic at 5% of the EU stream weight. Will enable prefix_cache and the smaller chunk size on the canary. Monitoring: p99 latency, token/sec per GPU, kv_miss_rate.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-45 — EU streaming burst — assigned to igor (priority: P2)
igor: Also adding a temporary QoS rule to throttle heavy non-streaming rerank jobs in EU to avoid noisy neighbours — will drop rerank concurrency from 20 -> 8 for 2h.
devon: FYI the rerank throttle command: `rctl set q:eu-rerank concurrency=8 --duration 2h`
elena: Financials OK with a controlled prewarm if it prevents p99 violations. Two options: prewarm 6x nodes for 24h (higher upfront) vs on-demand burst (higher per-token). Prewarm breakeven ~18h given current billing.
maya: Priorities for the next 60m: 1) start igor's canary, 2) enable prefix cache + TTL bump on canary, 3) apply chunk_size change on canary, 4) temporary rerank QoS. If canary looks good after 30m, roll incremental config to hosted-eu-stream.
priya: I'll prepare the config PR and include a quick eval harness to check hallucination/regression on smaller chunk sizes.
igor: Can confirm canary spin started (jobs queued). I'll post p99 and kv_miss_rate in this thread in ~20m.
maya: Thanks all — will pause the afternoon deploy if canary shows regressions. :thumbsup:
